items.title: PTSD may shape the human brain differently depending on gender, race and the age at which a person's trauma occurred
items.text: Stress and trauma can leave molecular marks in the brain that may help explain the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). A study published in the journal Cell Reports on Nov. 20 that examined the postmortem brains of 101 people with PTSD found that genes associated with PTSD varied more than expected across different brain regions when it comes to DNA methylation, a natural biological process that acts like a genetic "dimmer switch" for genes, sometimes blocking genetic code entirely.
